result: ## Summary I've implemented the CSS-based flat-lay composite feature for Similar Outfits as specified: **Work Completed:** - Created new `FlatLayComposite` component (`apps/web/components/outfit/FlatLayComposite.tsx` - 210 lines) that: - Accepts `items: Product[]` prop - Categorizes items into main garment, shoes, and accessories using case-insensitive matching - Positions main item (70% width) in center with slight rotation (-2deg) - Positions shoes (38% width) at bottom-left with -12deg rotation - Positions primary accessory (32% width) at top-right with 10deg rotation - Positions secondary accessory (28% width) at bottom-right with 5deg rotation - Uses `z-index` layering for overlapping effect - Applies `drop-shadow` for depth - Handles edge cases: empty items, single item, missing images, unclear categories - Updated `SimilarOutfits.tsx` to: - Import and use `FlatLayComposite` instead of `ProductThumbnailGrid` - Removed the old `ProductThumbnailGrid` component entirely - Falls back to `FlatLayComposite` when no `flatLayImageUrl` or `flatLayImageBase64` exists **Files Changed:** - `apps/web/components/outfit/FlatLayComposite.tsx` (new, 210 lines) - `apps/web/components/outfit/SimilarOutfits.tsx` (modified, reduced from ~85 lines to 54 lines) **Validation:** - Lint passes with only warnings (using `` instead of Next.js ``, consistent with existing codebase patterns) - Build has pre-existing unrelated errors (missing encoder.json in chat API)
